1	"""Fetch an Awesome-list README from GitHub and parse it.
  2	
  3	Resolves a GitHub repo URL to its raw README, trying the ``HEAD``, ``main``,
  4	and ``master`` refs in turn and falling back to the GitHub contents API if the
  5	raw host refuses. The raw markdown and the parsed structure are persisted into
  6	the run directory, and phase/artifact events are emitted when an event bus is
  7	supplied so the TUI and JSONL log see the work happen.
  8	"""
  9	
 10	from __future__ import annotations
 11	
 12	import base64
 13	import re
 14	from pathlib import Path
 15	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
 16	
 17	import httpx
 18	
 19	from awesome_researcher.core.events import EventType, make_event
 20	from awesome_researcher.parsers.markdown_parser import ParsedList, parse_markdown
 21	from awesome_researcher.utils.helpers import write_json
 22	
 23	if TYPE_CHECKING:
 24	    from awesome_researcher.config import Config
 25	    from awesome_researcher.core.events import EventBus
 26	
 27	_PHASE = "parse"
 28	_COMPONENT = "awesome_parser"
 29	
 30	# github.com/<owner>/<repo>[/...]; tolerates a trailing .git and extra path.
 31	_REPO_RE = re.compile(
 32	    r"github\.com[:/]+(?P<owner>[^/]+)/(?P<repo>[^/#?]+?)(?:\.git)?(?:[/#?].*)?$",
 33	    re.IGNORECASE,
 34	)
 35	
 36	# Refs to try on the raw host, in order.
 37	_REFS = ("HEAD", "main", "master")
 38	# README filename variants to try per ref.
 39	_READMES = ("README.md", "readme.md", "README.markdown", "Readme.md")
 40	
 41	
 42	class ReadmeFetchError(RuntimeError):
 43	    """Raised when no README could be retrieved through any strategy."""
 44	
 45	
 46	def parse_repo_url(repo_url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
 47	    """Extract ``(owner, repo)`` from a GitHub URL.
 48	
 49	    Raises ``ValueError`` if the URL is not a recognizable GitHub repo URL.
 50	    """
 51	
 52	    m = _REPO_RE.search((repo_url or "").strip())
 53	    if not m:
 54	        raise ValueError(f"not a GitHub repo URL: {repo_url!r}")
 55	    return m.group("owner"), m.group("repo")
 56	
 57	
 58	async def _emit(
 59	    event_bus: EventBus | None,
 60	    run_id: str,
 61	    correlation_id: str,
 62	    event_type: EventType,
 63	    *,
 64	    level: str = "INFO",
 65	    message: str = "",
 66	    metadata: dict | None = None,
 67	) -> None:
 68	    if event_bus is None:
 69	        return
 70	    await event_bus.publish(
 71	        make_event(
 72	            run_id,
 73	            event_type,
 74	            _COMPONENT,
 75	            phase=_PHASE,
 76	            level=level,
 77	            message=message,
 78	            correlation_id=correlation_id,
 79	            metadata=metadata or {},
 80	        )
 81	    )
 82	
 83	
 84	async def _fetch_readme_text(
 85	    client: httpx.AsyncClient,
 86	    owner: str,
 87	    repo: str,
 88	    config: Config,
 89	) -> tuple[str, str]:
 90	    """Return ``(markdown_text, source_url)`` for the repo's README.
 91	
 92	    Tries each raw ref/filename combination, then the contents API. Raises
 93	    :class:`ReadmeFetchError` if everything fails.
 94	    """
 95	
 96	    raw_base = config.github_raw_base.rstrip("/")
 97	    for ref in _REFS:
 98	        for fname in _READMES:
 99	            url = f"{raw_base}/{owner}/{repo}/{ref}/{fname}"
100	            try:
101	                resp = await client.get(url)
102	            except httpx.HTTPError:
103	                continue
104	            if resp.status_code == 200 and resp.text.strip():
105	                return resp.text, url
106	
107	    # Fallback: GitHub contents API returns base64-encoded content.
108	    api_base = config.github_api_base.rstrip("/")
109	    api_url = f"{api_base}/repos/{owner}/{repo}/readme"
110	    try:
111	        resp = await client.get(api_url, headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
112	        if resp.status_code == 200:
113	            payload = resp.json()
114	            content = payload.get("content", "")
115	            encoding = payload.get("encoding", "")
116	            if content and encoding == "base64":
117	                decoded = base64.b64decode(content).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
118	                if decoded.strip():
119	                    return decoded, api_url
120	    except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
121	        pass
122	
123	    raise ReadmeFetchError(f"could not fetch README for {owner}/{repo}")
124

126	async def fetch_and_parse(
127	    repo_url: str,
128	    run_dir: str | Path,
129	    config: Config,
130	    event_bus: EventBus | None = None,
131	    run_id: str = "",
132	    correlation_id: str = "",
133	) -> ParsedList:
134	    """Fetch ``repo_url``'s README, parse it, and persist the artifacts.
135	
136	    Writes ``original.md`` (raw markdown) and ``original.json`` (parsed) into
137	    ``run_dir`` and returns the :class:`ParsedList`. Emits PHASE_STARTED on
138	    entry, ARTIFACT_WRITTEN for each saved file, and PHASE_FINISHED on success.
139	    """
140	
141	    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
142	    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
143	    owner, repo = parse_repo_url(repo_url)
144	
145	    await _emit(
146	        event_bus,
147	        run_id,
148	        correlation_id,
149	        EventType.PHASE_STARTED,
150	        message=f"fetching README for {owner}/{repo}",
151	        metadata={"owner": owner, "repo": repo, "repo_url": repo_url},
152	    )
153	
154	    timeout = httpx.Timeout(config.http_timeout_seconds)
155	    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
156	        timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=True, headers={"User-Agent": "awesome-researcher"}
157	    ) as client:
158	        text, source_url = await _fetch_readme_text(client, owner, repo, config)
159	
160	    parsed = parse_markdown(text)
161	
162	    md_path = run_dir / "original.md"
163	    md_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
164	    await _emit(
165	        event_bus,
166	        run_id,
167	        correlation_id,
168	        EventType.ARTIFACT_WRITTEN,
169	        message="wrote original.md",
170	        metadata={"path": str(md_path), "source_url": source_url, "bytes": len(text)},
171	    )
172	
173	    json_path = run_dir / "original.json"
174	    write_json(json_path, parsed.to_dict())
175	    await _emit(
176	        event_bus,
177	        run_id,
178	        correlation_id,
179	        EventType.ARTIFACT_WRITTEN,
180	        message="wrote original.json",
181	        metadata={
182	            "path": str(json_path),
183	            "categories": len(parsed.categories),
184	            "items": parsed.item_count(),
185	        },
186	    )
187	
188	    await _emit(
189	        event_bus,
190	        run_id,
191	        correlation_id,
192	        EventType.PHASE_FINISHED,
193	        message=f"parsed {len(parsed.categories)} categories, {parsed.item_count()} items",
194	        metadata={"categories": len(parsed.categories), "items": parsed.item_count()},
195	    )
196	    return parsed

1	"""Render an updated Awesome-list Markdown that preserves the original structure.
  2	
  3	The renderer is the inverse of :mod:`awesome_researcher.parsers.markdown_parser`:
  4	it walks the parsed headings + items and re-emits them as a clean Markdown
  5	document, then appends the pipeline's accepted resources under the heading
  6	that matches the insert's target category. The original heading hierarchy
  7	(H2 -> H3 -> H4 ...) and the original item formatting (the ``- [Title](URL) -
  8	Description`` shape used by the parser) are preserved so an updated list reads
  9	identically to a hand-edited one and so ``awesome-lint`` keeps its verdict.
 10	
 11	New resources are inserted in the order provided, just below the existing
 12	items of the target category. When a target category does not exist in the
 13	original list the renderer appends a new H2 section at the end of the document
 14	for it (with a leading blank line so it renders cleanly in any viewer).
 15	"""
 16	
 17	from __future__ import annotations
 18	
 19	from collections.abc import Iterable
 20	from dataclasses import dataclass
 21	from pathlib import Path
 22	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
 23	
 24	from awesome_researcher.core.events import EventBus, EventType, make_event
 25	from awesome_researcher.parsers.markdown_parser import Category, ParsedItem, ParsedList
 26	
 27	if TYPE_CHECKING:
 28	    from awesome_researcher.config import Config
 29	
 30	
 31	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32	# Pure formatting helpers (offline-testable, no I/O, no events).
 33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 34	
 35	
 36	def _format_item(item: ParsedItem) -> str:
 37	    """Render one parsed item as the ``- [Title](URL) - Description`` shape."""
 38	
 39	    title = (item.title or "").strip()
 40	    url = (item.url or "").strip()
 41	    if not title or not url:
 42	        return ""
 43	    line = f"- [{title}]({url})"
 44	    if item.description:
 45	        line += f" - {item.description.strip()}"
 46	    return line
 47	
 48	
 49	def _heading_line(name: str, level: int) -> str:
 50	    """Render one heading as the ``#`` + space + name shape, clamped to 1-6."""
 51	
 52	    clamped = max(1, min(6, int(level)))
 53	    return f"{'#' * clamped} {name}"
 54	
 55	
 56	def _normalize(name: str) -> str:
 57	    return (name or "").strip().lower()
 58	
 59	
 60	@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
 61	class ResourceInsert:
 62	    """One new resource to inject under a target category.
 63	
 64	    ``category`` is matched (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped) against the
 65	    parsed ``Category.name`` field. A new top-level H2 section is appended at
 66	    the end of the rendered list when the target category is not present.
 67	    """
 68	
 69	    title: str
 70	    url: str
 71	    description: str = ""
 72	    category: str = ""
 73	
 74	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 75	        return {
 76	            "title": self.title,
 77	            "url": self.url,
 78	            "description": self.description,
 79	            "category": self.category,
 80	        }
 81	
 82	
 83	def _group_inserts_by_category(
 84	    inserts: Iterable[ResourceInsert],
 85	) -> dict[str, list[ResourceInsert]]:
 86	    """Bucket inserts by their target category (case-insensitive)."""
 87	
 88	    grouped: dict[str, list[ResourceInsert]] = {}
 89	    for insert in inserts:
 90	        key = _normalize(insert.category) or "(uncategorized)"
 91	        grouped.setdefault(key, []).append(insert)
 92	    return grouped
 93	
 94	
 95	def _format_insert(insert: ResourceInsert) -> str:
 96	    """Render one new insert in the same ``- [Title](URL) - Description`` shape."""
 97	
 98	    title = (insert.title or "").strip()
 99	    url = (insert.url or "").strip()
100	    if not title or not url:
101	        return ""
102	    line = f"- [{title}]({url})"
103	    if insert.description:
104	        line += f" - {insert.description.strip()}"
105	    return line

108	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
109	# The renderer.
110	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
111	
112	
113	class ListRenderer:
114	    """Render an updated Awesome list, preserving the original structure.
115	
116	    Usage::
117	
118	        renderer = ListRenderer(config, event_bus, run_id)
119	        markdown = renderer.render(parsed_list, [ResourceInsert(...)])
120	        await renderer.write(path, markdown, parsed_list, inserts)
121	    """
122	
123	    def __init__(
124	        self,
125	        config: Config | None = None,
126	        event_bus: EventBus | None = None,
127	        run_id: str = "",
128	    ) -> None:
129	        self._config = config
130	        self._event_bus = event_bus
131	        self._run_id = run_id
132	
133	    def render(
134	        self,
135	        parsed: ParsedList,
136	        inserts: Iterable[ResourceInsert] = (),
137	    ) -> str:
138	        """Return the updated Markdown for the parsed list + new inserts.
139	
140	        Empty / whitespace-only lines are dropped on the way out to keep the
141	        output diff-friendly. New items appear after the existing items of the
142	        matching category, separated by a single blank line.
143	        """
144	
145	        inserts_list = list(inserts)
146	        grouped = _group_inserts_by_category(inserts_list)
147	        out: list[str] = []
148	
149	        for cat in parsed.categories:
150	            out.append(_heading_line(cat.name, cat.level))
151	            for item in cat.items:
152	                line = _format_item(item)
153	                if line:
154	                    out.append(line)
155	            bucket = grouped.pop(_normalize(cat.name), None)
156	            if bucket:
157	                for insert in bucket:
158	                    line = _format_insert(insert)
159	                    if line:
160	                        out.append(line)
161	            out.append("")
162	
163	        # Any inserts whose target category was not seen in the original list
164	        # become fresh H2 sections appended at the end of the document.
165	        leftover = [ins for bucket in grouped.values() for ins in bucket]
166	        if leftover:
167	            leftover_by_name: dict[str, list[ResourceInsert]] = {}
168	            for ins in leftover:
169	                key = (ins.category or "Uncategorized").strip() or "Uncategorized"
170	                leftover_by_name.setdefault(key, []).append(ins)
171	            for name, bucket in leftover_by_name.items():
172	                out.append(_heading_line(name, 2))
173	                for ins in bucket:
174	                    line = _format_insert(ins)
175	                    if line:
176	                        out.append(line)
177	                out.append("")
178	
179	        # Strip trailing empty lines and ensure the file ends with one newline.
180	        while out and not out[-1].strip():
181	            out.pop()
182	        return ("\n".join(out) + "\n") if out else ""
183	
184	    async def write(
185	        self,
186	        path: str | Path,
187	        markdown: str,
188	        parsed: ParsedList,
189	        inserts: Iterable[ResourceInsert] = (),
190	    ) -> Path:
191	        """Render to ``path`` and emit an ``ARTIFACT_WRITTEN`` event."""
192	
193	        if not markdown:
194	            markdown = self.render(parsed, inserts)
195	        out = Path(path)
196	        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
197	        out.write_text(markdown, encoding="utf-8")
198	        if self._event_bus is not None:
199	            inserts_list = list(inserts)
200	            await self._event_bus.publish(
201	                make_event(
202	                    self._run_id,
203	                    EventType.ARTIFACT_WRITTEN,
204	                    "list_renderer",
205	                    phase="render",
206	                    message=f"wrote {out.name}",
207	                    metadata={
208	                        "path": str(out),
209	                        "bytes": len(markdown),
210	                        "inserts": len(inserts_list),
211	                        "categories": len(parsed.categories),
212	                        "items": parsed.item_count(),
213	                    },
214	                )
215	            )
216	        return out

219	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
220	# Source-preserving patcher: inject new items into the ORIGINAL text without
221	# reformatting any untouched byte. This is the strategy used for updated_list.md
222	# so a zero-insert run is byte-identical to the source README.
223	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
224	
225	
226	@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
227	class InsertionRecord:
228	    """One applied insertion, for the machine-readable manifest."""
229	
230	    title: str
231	    url: str
232	    category: str
233	    matched_category: str | None  # existing category name, or None if new section
234	    after_line: int  # 0-based source line index the item was inserted after
235	    text: str  # the exact line inserted
236	
237	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
238	        return {
239	            "title": self.title,
240	            "url": self.url,
241	            "category": self.category,
242	            "matched_category": self.matched_category,
243	            "after_line": self.after_line,
244	            "text": self.text,
245	        }

248	@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
249	class PatchResult:
250	    """The patched markdown plus the manifest of what was inserted."""
251	
252	    markdown: str
253	    inserted: list[InsertionRecord]
254	    unmatched: list[ResourceInsert]  # inserts whose category was not found
255	
256	    def manifest(self, *, source_bytes: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
257	        return {
258	            "strategy": "source-range-insertion",
259	            "source_bytes": source_bytes,
260	            "output_bytes": len(self.markdown.encode("utf-8")),
261	            "inserted_count": len(self.inserted),
262	            "unmatched_count": len(self.unmatched),
263	            "insertions": [r.to_dict() for r in self.inserted],
264	            "unmatched": [r.to_dict() for r in self.unmatched],

269	def _bullet_prefix(raw_line: str) -> str:
270	    """Extract the leading indent + bullet marker + one space from an item line.
271	
272	    Falls back to ``"- "`` so a category whose sample line is unavailable still
273	    renders a valid bullet.
274	    """
275	
276	    stripped = raw_line.lstrip()
277	    indent = raw_line[: len(raw_line) - len(stripped)]
278	    marker = stripped[:1] if stripped[:1] in "-*+" else "-"
279	    return f"{indent}{marker} "

282	class SourcePatcher:
283	    """Inject new resources into the original markdown, preserving every byte.
284	
285	    Contract:
286	      * Zero inserts -> output equals ``parsed.source_text`` byte for byte.
287	      * Each insert whose (normalized) category matches an existing
288	        ``Category`` is spliced in immediately after that category's last item
289	        line, matching the local bullet marker and indentation.
290	      * Inserts whose category is not found are collected as ``unmatched`` and
291	        appended as fresh ``## <category>`` sections at end-of-file; the caller
292	        may instead route them to review.
293	    """
294	
295	    def patch(
296	        self,
297	        parsed: ParsedList,
298	        inserts: Iterable[ResourceInsert] = (),
299	    ) -> PatchResult:
300	        inserts_list = list(inserts)
301	        lines = parsed.source_lines
302	        # Byte-identical fast path: nothing to insert.
303	        if not inserts_list:
304	            return PatchResult(markdown=parsed.source_text, inserted=[], unmatched=[])
305	
306	        # Map normalized category name -> its Category (last one wins on dupes).
307	        by_name: dict[str, Category] = {}
308	        for c in parsed.categories:

  2	
  3	Awesome lists are flat markdown: ``#``-level headings open categories and
  4	``- [Title](URL) - Description`` bullets list resources under them. We parse
  5	with ``re`` line by line rather than a full markdown AST because the relevant
  6	structure is shallow and the libraries (mistune/markdown) are not installed.
  7	
  8	What we KEEP: http(s) resource links that sit under a category heading.
  9	What we DROP: badge images ``![alt](src)`` and link-wrapped badges
 10	``[![alt](src)](href)``, the Table of Contents (in-page ``#anchor`` links),
 11	back-to-top links, italic category-description prose, and any HTML/inline-prose
 12	links. No-description links are retained with ``description=None`` — never
 13	dropped.
 14	"""
 15	
 16	from __future__ import annotations
 17	
 18	import re
 19	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 20	from typing import Any
 21	
 22	# A markdown heading: 1-6 leading hashes, then the title text.
 23	_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")
 24	
 25	# A list bullet (-, *, +) carrying a single markdown link, optionally followed
 26	# by a description after a hyphen or em dash. The link target is captured so we
 27	# can reject ``#anchor`` / image links downstream. ``[^\]]*`` for the title is
 28	# deliberately loose so titles containing punctuation still match; we exclude
 29	# image links explicitly via the leading ``!`` check.
 30	_ITEM_RE = re.compile(
 31	    r"""
 32	    ^\s*[-*+]\s+              # bullet marker
 33	    \[(?P<title>[^\]]*)\]     # [Title]
 34	    \((?P<url>[^)]+)\)        # (URL)
 35	    (?:\s*[-—:]\s*(?P<desc>.*\S))?  # optional ' - Description' / ' — ' / ' : '
 36	    \s*$
 37	    """,
 38	    re.VERBOSE,
 39	)
 40	
 41	# A bullet whose link is an image (badge) or a link-wrapped image (badge with a
 42	# click-through). Matched on the raw line so we can skip before _ITEM_RE.
 43	_BADGE_BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+\[?!\[")
 44

 47	class ParsedItem:
 48	    """A single resource link under a category."""
 49	
 50	    title: str
 51	    url: str
 52	    description: str | None

 78	    """

 81	    level: int

 83	    parent: str | None = None
 84	    is_leaf: bool = True

102	    """The whole parsed README: a flat ordered list of categories.
103	
104	    ``source_text`` is the exact original markdown; ``source_lines`` is its
105	    line split (kept without terminators). A source-preserving renderer uses
106	    these plus each category's ``last_item_line`` to inject new items while
107	    leaving every untouched byte identical.
108	    """

111	    source_text: str = ""
112	
113	    @property

116

118	        return {"categories": [c.to_dict() for c in self.categories]}

124	# Heading text that marks the table-of-contents / index section. Items under it
125	# are in-page anchors, not resources, and are skipped until the next heading.
126	_TOC_HEADINGS = {"contents", "table of contents", "toc", "index"}
127	
128

130	    """True only for http(s) links — excludes ``#anchor`` and ``mailto:`` etc."""
131	
132	    u = url.strip()
133	    return u.startswith("http://") or u.startswith("https://")
134	
135	
136	def _clean_title(title: str) -> str:
137	    """Strip surrounding markdown emphasis/backticks from a link title."""
138	
139	    t = title.strip()
140	    for marker in ("**", "__", "*", "_", "`"):
141	        if len(t) > 2 * len(marker) and t.startswith(marker) and t.endswith(marker):
142	            t = t[len(marker) : -len(marker)].strip()
143	    return t
144	
145	
146	def parse_markdown(text: str) -> ParsedList:
147	    """Parse Awesome-list markdown into a :class:`ParsedList`.
148	
149	    Headings open categories (tracking the ``#`` level); resource bullets are
150	    attached to the most recently opened category. The TOC section and any
151	    badge/anchor/HTML/prose links are excluded. Items keep ``description=None``
152	    when the bullet has no trailing description.
153	    """
154	
155	    categories: list[Category] = []
156	    current: Category | None = None
157	    in_toc = False
158	    # Stack of enclosing headings (innermost last) for parent resolution.
159	    stack: list[Category] = []
160	
161	    for lineno, raw_line in enumerate(text.splitlines() if text else []):
162	        line = raw_line.rstrip("\n")
163	
164	        heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
165	        if heading:
166	            level = len(heading.group(1))
167	            name = _clean_title(heading.group(2))
168	            # Entering or leaving the table of contents.
169	            in_toc = name.strip().lower() in _TOC_HEADINGS
170	            if in_toc:
171	                current = None
172	                continue
173	            # Pop any headings at the same or deeper level; the remaining top is
174	            # the nearest enclosing higher-level heading (the parent).
175	            while stack and stack[-1].level >= level:
176	                stack.pop()
177	            parent = stack[-1].name if stack else None
178	            current = Category(name=name, level=level, parent=parent, heading_line=lineno)
179	            categories.append(current)
180	            stack.append(current)
181	            continue
182	
183	        # Anything that is not a heading inside the TOC is an anchor list — skip.
184	        if in_toc or current is None:
185	            continue
186	
187	        # Skip badge bullets (image links / link-wrapped images) outright.
188	        if _BADGE_BULLET_RE.match(line):
189	            continue
190	
191	        item = _ITEM_RE.match(line)
192	        if not item:
193	            continue
194	
195	        url = item.group("url").strip()
196	        if not _is_resource_url(url):
197	            # In-page anchors, mailto, relative links — not resources.
198	            continue
199	
200	        title = _clean_title(item.group("title"))
201	        desc = item.group("desc")
202	        description = desc.strip() if desc and desc.strip() else None
203	        current.items.append(
204	            ParsedItem(
205	                title=title,
206	                url=url,
207	                description=description,
208	                raw_line=line.strip(),
209	            )
210	        )
211	        current.last_item_line = lineno
212	
213	    # A heading is a parent (is_leaf=False) when the next heading in document
214	    # order is deeper than it — its resources live in its sub-headings. The last
215	    # heading, and any followed only by same-or-higher headings, is a leaf.
216	    for idx, cat in enumerate(categories):
217	        nxt = categories[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(categories) else None
218	        cat.is_leaf = not (nxt is not None and nxt.level > cat.level)
219	
220	    return ParsedList(categories=categories, source_text=text or "")

def _extract_html_links(line: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str | None]]:
    """Extract resource links from a line containing inline HTML.

    Uses BeautifulSoup (``html.parser``) lazily so environments without bs4

    becomes the title; a trailing text node after a separator (``-``, ``—``,
    ``:``) becomes the description when present.

    except ImportError:

    try:

    except Exception:

        tail = ""

"""Byte-exact round-trip tests over the real Awesome-list fixtures.

For each committed fixture README, parse with :func:`parse_markdown`, then run
:class:`SourcePatcher` with zero inserts and require the output to equal the
source bytes exactly. Also verify each fixture parses non-trivially (>50
categories+items) and that a single inserted item changes only added lines
(diff via ``difflib``). Offline, real-fixture pattern of
``tests/test_phase3_parsers.py``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from awesome_researcher.parsers.markdown_parser import parse_markdown
from awesome_researcher.renderers.list_renderer import ResourceInsert, SourcePatcher

FIXTURES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"

FIXTURES = [
    "awesome-go.README.md",
    "awesome-python.README.md",
    "awesome-machine-learning.README.md",
]


def _fixture_path(name: str) -> Path:
    path = FIXTURES_DIR / name
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"fixture not present: {path}")
    return path


def _load(name: str) -> str:
    return _fixture_path(name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_zero_insert_round_trip_is_byte_identical(name):
    source = _load(name)
    parsed = parse_markdown(source)
    result = SourcePatcher().patch(parsed)
    assert result.markdown == source
    assert result.inserted == []
    assert result.unmatched == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_fixture_parses_non_trivially(name):
    parsed = parse_markdown(_load(name))
    total = len(parsed.categories) + parsed.item_count()
    assert total > 50, f"{name}: only {total} categories+items parsed"
    assert parsed.item_count() > 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_single_insert_changes_only_added_lines(name):
    source = _load(name)
    parsed = parse_markdown(source)

    # Pick a real category that has at least one item so the insert anchors
    # after an existing bullet.
    target = next(
        (c for c in parsed.categories if c.items), None
    )
    assert target is not None, f"{name}: no category with items to anchor on"

    insert = ResourceInsert(
        title="Round Trip Probe",
        url="https://example.com/round-trip-probe",
        description="Temporary probe resource.",
        category=target.name,
    )
    result = SourcePatcher().patch(parsed, [insert])
    assert len(result.inserted) == 1
    assert result.unmatched == []

    diff = list(
        difflib.unified_diff(
            source.splitlines(),
            result.markdown.splitlines(),
            lineterm="",
            n=0,
        )
    )
    added = [l for l in diff if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++")]
    removed = [l for l in diff if l.startswith("-") and not l.startswith("---")]

    # Only additions: every original line survives unchanged.
    assert removed == [], f"{name}: insertion removed lines: {removed}"
    assert len(added) == 1
    assert "Round Trip Probe" in added[0]

"""Line-based parser for Awesome-list README markdown.

Awesome lists are flat markdown: ``#``-level headings open categories and
``- [Title](URL) - Description`` bullets list resources under them. We parse
with ``re`` line by line rather than a full markdown AST because the relevant
structure is shallow and the libraries (mistune/markdown) are not installed.

What we KEEP: http(s) resource links that sit under a category heading.
What we DROP: badge images ``![alt](src)`` and link-wrapped badges
``[![alt](src)](href)``, the Table of Contents (in-page ``#anchor`` links),
back-to-top links, italic category-description prose, and any HTML/inline-prose
links. No-description links are retained with ``description=None`` — never
dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

# A markdown heading: 1-6 leading hashes, then the title text.
_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")

# A list bullet (-, *, +) carrying a single markdown link, optionally followed
# by a description after a hyphen or em dash. The link target is captured so we
# can reject ``#anchor`` / image links downstream. ``[^\]]*`` for the title is
# deliberately loose so titles containing punctuation still match; we exclude
# image links explicitly via the leading ``!`` check.
_ITEM_RE = re.compile(
    r"""
    ^\s*[-*+]\s+              # bullet marker
    \[(?P<title>[^\]]*)\]     # [Title]
    \((?P<url>[^)]+)\)        # (URL)
    (?:\s*[-—:]\s*(?P<desc>.*\S))?  # optional ' - Description' / ' — ' / ' : '
    \s*$
    """,
    re.VERBOSE,
)

# A bullet whose link is an image (badge) or a link-wrapped image (badge with a
# click-through). Matched on the raw line so we can skip before _ITEM_RE.
_BADGE_BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+\[?!\[")


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ParsedItem:
    """A single resource link under a category."""

    title: str
    url: str
    description: str | None
    raw_line: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "title": self.title,
            "url": self.url,
            "description": self.description,
            "raw_line": self.raw_line,
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Category:
    """A heading plus the resource items collected beneath it.

    ``parent`` is the name of the nearest enclosing higher-level heading (None
    for a top-level heading); ``is_leaf`` is False when a deeper sub-heading
    appears before the next same-or-higher heading. Both are computed from the
    level sequence so the renderer can reconstruct the heading tree and insert a
    new link under the correct existing heading.

    ``heading_line`` / ``last_item_line`` are 0-based indices into the source
    line list. ``last_item_line`` is the anchor a source-preserving renderer
    inserts *after* to add a new resource without disturbing any other byte; it
    stays ``-1`` for a heading with no items.
    """

    name: str
    level: int
    items: list[ParsedItem] = field(default_factory=list)
    parent: str | None = None
    is_leaf: bool = True
    heading_line: int = -1
    last_item_line: int = -1

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "level": self.level,
            "parent": self.parent,
            "is_leaf": self.is_leaf,
            "heading_line": self.heading_line,
            "last_item_line": self.last_item_line,
            "items": [it.to_dict() for it in self.items],
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ParsedList:
    """The whole parsed README: a flat ordered list of categories.

    ``source_text`` is the exact original markdown; ``source_lines`` is its
    line split (kept without terminators). A source-preserving renderer uses
    these plus each category's ``last_item_line`` to inject new items while
    leaving every untouched byte identical.
    """

    categories: list[Category] = field(default_factory=list)
    source_text: str = ""

    @property
    def source_lines(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.source_text.splitlines()

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"categories": [c.to_dict() for c in self.categories]}

    def item_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(len(c.items) for c in self.categories)


# Heading text that marks the table-of-contents / index section. Items under it
# are in-page anchors, not resources, and are skipped until the next heading.
_TOC_HEADINGS = {"contents", "table of contents", "toc", "index"}


def _is_resource_url(url: str) -> bool:
    """True only for http(s) links — excludes ``#anchor`` and ``mailto:`` etc."""

    u = url.strip()
    return u.startswith("http://") or u.startswith("https://")


def _clean_title(title: str) -> str:
    """Strip surrounding markdown emphasis/backticks from a link title."""

    t = title.strip()
    for marker in ("**", "__", "*", "_", "`"):
        if len(t) > 2 * len(marker) and t.startswith(marker) and t.endswith(marker):
            t = t[len(marker) : -len(marker)].strip()
    return t


def parse_markdown(text: str) -> ParsedList:
    """Parse Awesome-list markdown into a :class:`ParsedList`.

    Headings open categories (tracking the ``#`` level); resource bullets are
    attached to the most recently opened category. The TOC section and any
    badge/anchor/HTML/prose links are excluded. Items keep ``description=None``
    when the bullet has no trailing description.
    """

    categories: list[Category] = []
    current: Category | None = None
    in_toc = False
    # Stack of enclosing headings (innermost last) for parent resolution.
    stack: list[Category] = []

    for lineno, raw_line in enumerate(text.splitlines() if text else []):
        line = raw_line.rstrip("\n")

        heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if heading:
            level = len(heading.group(1))
            name = _clean_title(heading.group(2))
            # Entering or leaving the table of contents.
            in_toc = name.strip().lower() in _TOC_HEADINGS
            if in_toc:
                current = None
                continue
            # Pop any headings at the same or deeper level; the remaining top is
            # the nearest enclosing higher-level heading (the parent).
            while stack and stack[-1].level >= level:
                stack.pop()
            parent = stack[-1].name if stack else None
            current = Category(name=name, level=level, parent=parent, heading_line=lineno)
            categories.append(current)
            stack.append(current)
            continue

        # Anything that is not a heading inside the TOC is an anchor list — skip.
        if in_toc or current is None:
            continue

        # Skip badge bullets (image links / link-wrapped images) outright.
        if _BADGE_BULLET_RE.match(line):
            continue

        item = _ITEM_RE.match(line)
        if not item:
            continue

        url = item.group("url").strip()
        if not _is_resource_url(url):
            # In-page anchors, mailto, relative links — not resources.
            continue

        title = _clean_title(item.group("title"))
        desc = item.group("desc")
        description = desc.strip() if desc and desc.strip() else None
        current.items.append(
            ParsedItem(
                title=title,
                url=url,
                description=description,
                raw_line=line.strip(),
            )
        )
        current.last_item_line = lineno

    # A heading is a parent (is_leaf=False) when the next heading in document
    # order is deeper than it — its resources live in its sub-headings. The last
    # heading, and any followed only by same-or-higher headings, is a leaf.
    for idx, cat in enumerate(categories):
        nxt = categories[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(categories) else None
        cat.is_leaf = not (nxt is not None and nxt.level > cat.level)

    return ParsedList(categories=categories, source_text=text or "")

        line, matching the local bullet marker and indentation.

        may instead route them to review.

    def patch(
        self,
        parsed: ParsedList,
        inserts: Iterable[ResourceInsert] = (),
    ) -> PatchResult:
        inserts_list = list(inserts)
        lines = parsed.source_lines
        # Byte-identical fast path: nothing to insert.
        if not inserts_list:
            return PatchResult(markdown=parsed.source_text, inserted=[], unmatched=[])

        by_name: dict[str, Category] = {}
        for c in parsed.categories:

        # anchor_line -> list[(record-fields)] to splice AFTER that line.
        pending: dict[int, list[tuple[str, ResourceInsert, str]]] = {}
        inserted: list[InsertionRecord] = []
        unmatched: list[ResourceInsert] = []

        for ins in inserts_list:
            cat: Category | None = by_name.get(_normalize(ins.category))
            if cat is None:
                unmatched.append(ins)
                continue

            anchor = cat.last_item_line if cat.last_item_line >= 0 else cat.heading_line

FIXTURES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"

FIXTURES = [
    "awesome-go.README.md",
    "awesome-python.README.md",
    "awesome-machine-learning.README.md",
]


def _load(name: str) -> str:
    path = FIXTURES_DIR / name
    assert path.exists(), f"missing fixture: {path}"
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def _leaf_category_with_items(parsed):
    """Pick a real leaf category holding at least one item."""
    for cat in parsed.categories:
        if cat.is_leaf and cat.items and cat.last_item_line >= 0:
            return cat
    return None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_zero_insert_round_trip_is_byte_identical(name):
    source = _load(name)
    parsed = parse_markdown(source)
    result = SourcePatcher().patch(parsed, inserts=[])
    assert result.inserted == []
    assert result.unmatched == []
    assert result.markdown == source


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_fixture_yields_nontrivial_parse(name):
    parsed = parse_markdown(_load(name))
    assert len(parsed.categories) + parsed.item_count() > 50
    assert parsed.item_count() > 0
    assert any(cat.is_leaf and cat.items for cat in parsed.categories)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", FIXTURES)
def test_single_insert_changes_only_added_lines(name):
    source = _load(name)
    parsed = parse_markdown(source)
    cat = _leaf_category_with_items(parsed)
    assert cat is not None, "fixture has no leaf category with items"

    insert = ResourceInsert(
        title="Round-Tip Probe",
        url="https://example.com/round-tip-probe",
        description="Inserted by the round-trip test.",
        category=cat.name,
    )
    result = SourcePatcher().patch(parsed, inserts=[insert])
    assert len(result.inserted) == 1
    assert result.unmatched == []

    diff = list(
        difflib.unified_diff(
            source.splitlines(keepends=True),
            result.markdown.splitlines(keepends=True),
            n=0,
        )
    )
    added = [l for l in diff if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++")]
    removed = [l for l in diff if l.startswith("-") and not l.startswith("---")]

    # The insert landed immediately after the category's last item line.

    # Removing the inserted line restores the source exactly.

    restored = patched_lines[: rec.after_line + 1] + patched_lines[rec.after_line + 2 :]
